ideas.title: Scoped borrowing and escape checks
ideas.pitch: Catch references that outlive their storage.
ideas.experience: Reject a returned stack reference or a reference-capturing closure stored past its frame. Start with bounded checks rather than full lifetime inference.
ideas.how: Extend analysis of local references, borrowed spans and by-reference captures; validate with compiler examples and Nelibc buffers.
ideas.risks: Aliases through raw pointers, imported C and calls need explicit boundaries; bounded checking is not a memory safety proof.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Function capability contracts
ideas.pitch: State which functions may allocate, block or call platform services.
ideas.experience: An allocator helper or signal handler reports the exact call that introduces a forbidden dependency.
ideas.how: Check explicit contracts transitively across known callees; require declared contracts at foreign and indirect-call boundaries.
ideas.risks: Separate allocation, blocking and platform effects precisely; unknown callbacks must not silently count as safe.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Resource typestate
ideas.pitch: Make legal resource transitions visible in types.
ideas.experience: An open handle can be read; a closed handle cannot. Starting a device queue consumes its configured state.
ideas.how: Prototype owned wrappers with distinct state types before deciding whether compiler support is needed.
ideas.risks: Error recovery and partially completed transitions must preserve ownership without excessive wrapper code.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Caller-supplied storage
ideas.pitch: Use bounded output and scratch buffers consistently.
ideas.experience: A formatter or parser accepts your storage and reports required capacity or useful partial progress.
ideas.how: Design library conventions for spans, scratch regions, allocator choice and failure semantics; try Nelibc formatting wrappers.
ideas.risks: Partial writes and required-size reporting need precise contracts. Existing spans do not establish storage lifetime.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Named variant cases
ideas.pitch: Distinguish alternatives even when their payload types match.
ideas.experience: Read(fd) and Write(fd) are separate cases with the same descriptor representation.
ideas.how: Extend variant construction and exhaustive match to named cases; prove it on protocol messages and parser nodes.
ideas.risks: Define namespacing, zero initialization and compatibility with existing type-based variants.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Distinct types and controlled conversions
ideas.pitch: Keep descriptors, byte counts, pages and addresses apart.
ideas.experience: Adding a byte count to an address is permitted; adding two file descriptors is rejected.
ideas.how: Prototype distinct wrappers and selected operators, then assess a representation-preserving type declaration.
ideas.risks: Define explicit conversion, ABI, generic matching and which operations preserve the distinct type.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Explicit checked arithmetic
ideas.pitch: Choose checked, wrapping or saturating operations deliberately.
ideas.experience: Compute allocation count times element size and handle overflow before reserving memory.
ideas.how: Provide consistent integer operations and checked narrowing; align compile-time evaluation with generated C.
ideas.risks: Signed overflow, target widths and conversion edges must have defined semantics in both evaluators.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Typed errors and propagation
ideas.pitch: Preserve failure information with Result(T, E).
ideas.experience: A parser distinguishes invalid input, truncated input and insufficient output capacity, with exhaustive handling.
ideas.how: Start with a variant-backed library and explore propagation that composes with existing optional question-mark syntax.
ideas.risks: Success and error payloads may have the same type; propagation and owned payload cleanup need clear rules.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Binary layout descriptions
ideas.pitch: Describe byte order, field widths and validation together.
ideas.experience: Parse ELF or TZif data and packets without treating wire bytes as native structs.
ideas.how: Generate bounded readers and writers from a compile-time schema; verify offsets independently of native C layout.
ideas.risks: Unaligned access, malformed lengths, overflow and versioned formats require explicit behavior.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Validated compile-time platform descriptions
ideas.pitch: Build and validate static platform configuration in one place.
ideas.experience: A platform without a clock explicitly rejects timed waits or selects an unsupported-operation implementation.
ideas.how: Extend typed compile-time configuration into callback validation, operation tables and generated bindings; try Nelibc host operations.
ideas.risks: Distinguish an absent capability from a runtime failure. Keep the core independent of workshop consumers.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Typed hardware memory access
ideas.pitch: Give device registers access rules beyond ordinary memory.
ideas.experience: A write-only register cannot be read, and a write-one-to-clear register gets an appropriate operation.
ideas.how: Prototype register accessors with widths and permissions; add compiler support only where emission guarantees require it.
ideas.risks: Volatile access is not an atomic or ordering guarantee. Architecture-specific barriers and exact access widths need validation.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Relative references into regions
ideas.pitch: Store checked offsets instead of process-specific pointers.
ideas.experience: Move or map a data structure at a new base and resolve its references against an explicit region.
ideas.how: Prototype region-bound offsets and checked resolution for shared memory or mapped data.
ideas.risks: Region identity, alignment, overflow, mutation and temporary pointer lifetime all need contracts.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Typed protocol and state-machine descriptions
ideas.pitch: Describe states, messages and legal transitions together.
ideas.experience: A protocol handler handles every legal input and makes forbidden transitions explicit.
ideas.how: Use syntax extensions and compile-time generation of ordinary records and dispatch; start with a small incremental protocol.
ideas.risks: Define failure transitions, ownership and async boundaries; avoid claiming that a generated machine verifies the whole protocol.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Generators with visible storage
ideas.pitch: Suspend and resume a function through a caller-owned state record.
ideas.experience: An incremental parser resumes as bytes arrive without a separate stack or implicit heap allocation.
ideas.how: Lower suspension points into explicit state and lifecycle operations with a documented layout policy.
ideas.risks: Ownership, references across suspension, cleanup and cancellation are major design questions.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Typed holes for development
ideas.pitch: Ask the compiler what belongs in an unfinished expression.
ideas.experience: A placeholder reports the expected type, available bindings and unmet generic constraints.
ideas.how: Add a diagnostic-only placeholder that cannot enter an executable; try it in generic and compile-time examples.
ideas.risks: Keep suggestions bounded and accurate in the presence of forward inference and unresolved types.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Content-addressed definitions
ideas.pitch: Give code a stable identity beyond its file and spelling.
ideas.experience: Rename or move a helper without changing its identity; inspect exactly which implementation and dependencies a program uses.
ideas.how: Prototype an optional index of canonical, resolved typed definitions and dependency hashes. Keep text files as the editing format and C as an output. Derive artifact-cache keys separately from code identity, target, toolchain and build inputs. Inspiration: Unison content-addressed definitions.
ideas.risks: Hash equality is not behavioral equivalence. Recursive groups, nominal type identity, macros and mutable globals need explicit rules. Foreign implementation versions and exported ABI names must be accounted for; a source hash does not pin a host libc.
ideas.audience: Nelua compiler, Nelibc, firmware and systems-tool developers

ideas.title: Dependency-aware upgrade plans
ideas.pitch: Treat an upgrade as an explicit change to a code graph.
ideas.experience: Preview every caller affected by replacing one parser definition, retain the old version, and inspect failed type checks before applying the upgrade.
ideas.how: Use stable definition identities to map old dependencies to replacements; recheck affected users and let the developer accept a reviewable patch. Start with a Nelibc helper upgrade.
ideas.risks: Matching types does not prove matching behavior. Preserve tests and ABI checks; coexistence of native versions needs symbol isolation, and patches must not silently change global state.
ideas.audience: Nelua compiler, Nelibc, firmware and systems-tool developers

ideas.title: Structural code queries and refactoring
ideas.pitch: Search and transform resolved code rather than matching spelling.
ideas.experience: Find every call to a particular imported operation even when it has aliases, then preview a typed replacement across the project.
ideas.how: Expose a read-only typed-code query API first, then transactional rewrite plans with source locations, hygiene and type checking. A content-addressed index can supply stable references.
ideas.risks: Generated syntax, macro provenance and formatting complicate rewriting. Identity alone does not prove a rewrite correct; always expose the resulting source diff.
ideas.audience: Nelua compiler, Nelibc, firmware and systems-tool developers

ideas.title: Portable computation capsules
ideas.pitch: Package an explicitly portable function and its inputs for another machine.
ideas.experience: Send a pure packet-analysis task to a build server; it resolves the exact code dependencies and returns a typed result.
ideas.how: Define a restricted portable subset with canonical value encoding, a dependency manifest and an explicit remote executor. Compile or locate a native artifact for the destination target rather than sending raw process memory.
ideas.risks: Ordinary pointers, file handles and C imports cannot travel implicitly. Code identity grants no authority or sandbox: admission, execution limits, authentication and target compatibility are separate requirements.
ideas.audience: Nelua compiler, Nelibc, firmware and systems-tool developers

ideas.category: Nelua · Effects, time and changing programs
ideas.title: Algebraic effects and handlers
ideas.pitch: Write a clock or storage request once; choose its implementation around the call.
ideas.experience: Run the same state machine against a real clock, a simulated clock or a deterministic test log.
ideas.how: Explore typed effect requests and lexical handlers as a separate proposal from capability restrictions. Begin with non-resuming or single-resumption handlers that lower to explicit context records and calls. Inspiration: Unison abilities.
ideas.risks: Resuming a continuation interacts with stack references, ownership and cleanup. Multiple resumption needs a separate design; imports and callbacks cannot claim undeclared effects are absent.
ideas.audience: Nelua compiler, Nelibc, firmware and systems-tool developers

ideas.category: Nelua · Effects, time and changing programs
ideas.title: Deterministic record and replay
ideas.pitch: Turn a hard-to-reproduce systems failure into a replayable input trace.
ideas.experience: Capture clock, randomness and platform-operation results, then rerun a protocol state machine from the same starting state.
ideas.how: Record at declared effect or platform boundaries; version trace schemas and code identities. Start with a single-threaded Nelibc host consumer before addressing scheduling.
ideas.risks: Raw C, MMIO and unrecorded I/O break determinism. Replay must suppress external writes; concurrent scheduling and sensitive trace data require explicit policies.
ideas.audience: Nelua compiler, Nelibc, firmware and systems-tool developers

ideas.category: Nelua · Effects, time and changing programs
ideas.title: Durable functions that survive restarts
ideas.pitch: Persist progress at deliberate suspension boundaries.
ideas.experience: A firmware update coordinator resumes after a power loss without repeating an already acknowledged step.
ideas.how: Lower an opt-in function into a versioned state machine with serializable locals, explicit durable storage and logged effect receipts. Build on visible generator storage rather than serializing a native stack.
ideas.risks: Exactly-once external effects require cooperation or reconciliation, not just a saved continuation. Upgrades need migrations; pointers and live locks cannot be persisted as ordinary locals.
ideas.audience: Nelua compiler, Nelibc, firmware and systems-tool developers

ideas.category: Nelua · Effects, time and changing programs
ideas.title: Live patching with state migration
ideas.pitch: Replace a running component at a declared safe point.
ideas.experience: Change a long-running host tool or simulator while preserving state through an explicit migration function.
ideas.how: Start in hosted user-space with versioned dispatch tables, quiescence points, layout checks and opt-in state migrations. Keep static freestanding builds on their existing path.
ideas.risks: Active frames, borrowed references, TLS and old callbacks can retain the prior implementation. Define rollback and reclamation; matching hashes or ABI layouts alone do not make a patch safe.
ideas.audience: Nelua compiler, Nelibc, firmware and systems-tool developers

ideas.category: Nelua · Effects, time and changing programs
ideas.title: Incremental computations
ideas.pitch: Recompute only the pure derived values affected by an input change.
ideas.experience: Adjust one device configuration field and refresh the dependent tables and diagnostics while retaining unrelated work.
ideas.how: Prototype a library of explicit input cells and pure dependency-tracked computations with invalidation and bounded caches. Explore compiler assistance only after a concrete consumer.
ideas.risks: Hidden mutation and effects invalidate cached results. Cycles, cache lifetimes and deterministic dependency discovery need rules; this does not make arbitrary Nelua code reactive.
ideas.audience: Nelua compiler, Nelibc, firmware and systems-tool developers

ideas.title: Partial evaluation and specialization
ideas.pitch: Fix part of a program input and generate a smaller specialized function.
ideas.experience: Specialize a packet decoder for a known schema while leaving packet bytes as runtime input.
ideas.how: Explore an opt-in specialization operation over typed code, with explicit static arguments and code-size budgets; emit ordinary Nelua IR and C. This goes beyond folding a call whose result is entirely known.
ideas.risks: Prevent specialization explosions and preserve overflow, aliasing and evaluation-order semantics. Foreign calls and effects limit what may be evaluated early.
ideas.audience: Nelua compiler, Nelibc, firmware and systems-tool developers

ideas.title: Bounded refinement constraints
ideas.pitch: Carry simple facts such as ranges and alignment with a value.
ideas.experience: A validated packet length can be passed to a bounded decoder without losing the fact that it fits the buffer.
ideas.how: Start with integer ranges, alignment and constant relationships at function boundaries. Discharge a small decidable subset statically and require explicit validation for the rest.
ideas.risks: A length fact does not establish pointer validity or lifetime. Mutation can invalidate relationships; define runtime-check behavior and avoid pretending a general theorem prover is available.
ideas.audience: Nelua compiler, Nelibc, firmware and systems-tool developers

ideas.title: Session-typed communication endpoints
ideas.pitch: Check both sides of a message exchange against their protocol.
ideas.experience: A worker must receive configuration before sending a result, and consuming an endpoint advances its permitted operations.
ideas.how: Represent protocol states and dual endpoints using owned types first; generate typed send and receive operations over an explicit transport. Prototype an in-process worker exchange.
ideas.risks: Message loss, cancellation, branching and protocol upgrades need explicit outcomes. Static sequencing alone does not guarantee deadlock freedom or reliable delivery.
ideas.audience: Nelua compiler, Nelibc, firmware and systems-tool developers

ideas.title: Typed address spaces
ideas.pitch: Keep CPU, device, DMA and remote addresses distinct.
ideas.experience: A device-visible DMA address cannot accidentally be dereferenced as a CPU pointer; mapping it requires the platform capability.
ideas.how: Prototype distinct address-space parameters and explicit map/unmap APIs around existing pointers. Later assess backend support for targets with separate memory spaces.
ideas.risks: An address-space tag does not perform cache synchronization, grant access or establish lifetime. IOMMU mappings, ownership and target-specific representations remain explicit contracts.
ideas.audience: Nelua compiler, Nelibc, firmware and systems-tool developers

ideas.title: Transactional region snapshots
ideas.pitch: Checkpoint an owned data region and reopen a consistent version.
ideas.experience: A simulator or embedded state store commits a new graph of records and recovers the previous valid snapshot after an interrupted write.
ideas.how: Combine region-relative references, versioned schemas and copy-on-write or journaled updates. Begin with a user-space file-backed library and fault-injection tests.
ideas.risks: Crash consistency depends on actual storage ordering and flush guarantees. External effects cannot be rolled back with memory; concurrent writers and migrations need defined protocols.
ideas.audience: Nelua compiler, Nelibc, firmware and systems-tool developers

ideas.title: Declarative logic rules
ideas.pitch: Describe derived facts and let a bounded rule engine find the consequences.
ideas.experience: Derive which platform operations or device dependencies are reachable, and show the chain of facts behind an answer.
ideas.how: Prototype a syntax-extension library for typed facts and monotone rules compiled into explicit worklists and indexed tables; use it on a small platform configuration.
ideas.risks: Require finite domains or resource bounds. Negation, deletion and incremental updates need defined semantics; rule evaluation may allocate unless storage is explicitly supplied.
ideas.audience: Nelua compiler, Nelibc, firmware and systems-tool developers
